calls.head: Talbot’s hold on the Panthers won’t last
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Talbot has been a wall against the Panthers, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Panthers finally get to him.

calls.head: The Blue Jackets can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Blue Jackets’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Panthers’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Blue Jackets tonight.

calls.beyond: Florida has a better power play than most, and Columbus has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 4 power-play goals on 6 chances. A power play like theirs against a kill like Columbus’s scores 4 or more about once every 20 games.

story.head: A natural hat trick for Brady Tkachuk
paras: Kent Johnson got the scoring started for the Blue Jackets midway through the first. The second period belonged to the Panthers. Brady Tkachuk scored his first goal for Florida early in the period to tie it 1-1. Brady Tkachuk scored again on the power play three and a half minutes later to put the Panthers ahead 2-1. Brady Tkachuk completed a natural hat trick on the power play four and a half minutes later to make it 3-1. Carter Verhaeghe made it 4-1 on the power play late in the second. The third period brought five goals. Sam Reinhart and Verhaeghe scored just over two minutes apart early in the period to stretch the lead to 6-1. Columbus pulled Cam Talbot after six goals and turned to Jet Greaves for the rest of the third. Denton Mateychuk and Cole Sillinger scored 22 seconds apart with a little over six minutes left to cut Florida’s lead to 6-3. Reinhart scored again into the empty net with a little over two minutes left. His brother Matthew Tkachuk assisted on all three, and had five assists in all. Seth Jones finished with four assists, and Reinhart added an assist for a three-point night.
The chances were closer than the score. Akira Schmid made 24 saves for the Panthers.

The Panthers scored four power-play goals on six chances. Mathieu Olivier was thrown out with a game misconduct midway through the second. The Cats improved to 3-2-2 and climbed to fourth in the Atlantic, while the Blue Jackets dropped to 2-3-0, slipping to seventh in the Metropolitan.
